items.title: Get to the source of the problem.
items.description: A ceiling stain, missing shingles or damaged flashing can point to very different repairs. Start by understanding where the damage is and how the surrounding roof is holding up.

items.title: Plan more than a change of shingles.
items.description: A replacement is a chance to consider the roof as a complete system. Compare the material, preparation, installation details and written coverage alongside the finished appearance.
items.detail: Explore the replacement page before discussing your project. Ask what the estimate includes, how the existing covering will be removed and how any underlying damage would be addressed.
items.label: Explore roof replacement

items.title: Put the price in the context of your roof.
items.description: Roof dimensions, slope, access, material choice and the work beneath the covering can all change the scope. A useful comparison starts with what each estimate actually includes.
items.detail: Use the roof-cost guide to prepare questions for a project-specific estimate. Discuss removal, preparation, cleanup and how additional work would be agreed upon before treating two prices as equivalent.

items.title: Start exploring your project budget.

items.title: Think in terms of a complete GAF system.
items.description: Shingles are the visible surface, but the proposed installation also needs to address underlayment, flashing, ventilation and compatible accessories.
items.detail: Explore our GAF roofing information, then compare the product pages for colors and published specifications. Ask which products and warranty options are included in the exact system proposed for your home.
items.label: Explore GAF roofing installation

items.title: Understand the certification behind the company.
items.description: Roof King & Restoration holds GAF Master Elite certification. Learn what that designation means and how it relates to qualifying GAF roof systems.
items.detail: Certification and warranty coverage are different questions. Review the specific products, eligibility requirements and written terms with the team rather than assuming every project carries the same coverage.
items.label: Explore Master Elite certification

items.title: Explore a different roof finish.
items.description: If you are considering metal roofing, compare the proposed system with the shape, details and appearance of your home. There is more to the decision than the surface color.
items.detail: Our metal roofing page introduces the service. Discuss the available profiles and finishes, installation requirements and written warranty alongside your other material options.
items.label: Explore metal roofing

items.title: Make sense of what a storm left behind.
items.description: Wind and hail can cause damage that is not obvious from the ground. Discuss an inspection so you can understand the roof condition and the restoration work it may need.
items.detail: Share when you noticed the problem and any photos you can take safely from the ground. The storm restoration page explains the service; insurance coverage depends on your policy and insurer.
items.label: Explore storm restoration

decision.title: Start with answers. Then make a decision.
paragraphs: You shouldn’t have to decide on a new roof before you understand the one you have. A leak may be limited to one area; recurring problems or widespread wear can point to a bigger conversation.
Talk through the roof’s condition, previous repairs and the proposed work. A useful estimate explains the recommendation and gives you something concrete to compare.
items: Water marks or an active leak
A recent wind or hail event
An older roof you want evaluated

local.title: A local team. A conversation about your home.
local.description: Roof King & Restoration is based in Columbus. Talk with our team about your address, the condition of your roof and the work you have in mind. If you have photos or details of previous repairs, bring those to the conversation.

items.question: Does a leak mean I need a new roof?

children.text: Not necessarily. The location of the problem, surrounding roof condition and repair history all matter. An inspection helps you discuss whether a localized repair or broader work makes sense.

items.question: What should I compare in roofing estimates?

children.text: Compare the scope of removal and preparation, exact materials, installation details, cleanup and written coverage. Ask how changes or additional work discovered during the project would be handled.

items.question: Can I compare shingles and metal roofing?

children.text: Yes. Explore our shingle product library and metal roofing information, then ask which systems suit your home. Compare the complete installation scope and product-specific terms, not just the visible finish.

Roof King publishes five-year workmanship coverage. Manufacturer warranties apply separately to the selected products or eligible systems. Review the written terms and eligibility for the exact project in your estimate.

items.question: What if I noticed damage after a storm?

children.text: Contact the team to discuss an inspection and share what you can observe safely from the ground. Inspection findings can inform the proposed repair or restoration work. Insurance coverage depends on your policy and insurer.
Yes. Ask for current options, then review lender rates, approval requirements and repayment terms before you apply. Available financing does not replace a project-specific estimate.
